forces.title: New GST Framework Sustains High Tax Burden on Tobacco
forces.description: The 56th GST Council meeting introduced a new two-tiered GST structure, including a special de-merit rate of 40% for sin goods, which directly impacts tobacco products. Furthermore, existing GST rates and compensation cess on specific tobacco products (pan masala, gutkha, cigarettes, chewing tobacco, unmanufactured tobacco, and bidis) will continue. This continuation is mandated until compensation cess account obligations are met, anticipated in H2 FY26. This sustained high taxation, coupled with the new de-merit rate, represents a significant structural headwind for the tobacco industry, contrasting with tax reductions for numerous other goods.

viewpoints.title: Tobacco products face persistent high taxation and de-merit classification
viewpoints.description: CareEdge's analysis of the GST reforms in September 2025 indicates that specific tobacco products (pan masala, gutkha, cigarettes, chewing tobacco, unmanufactured tobacco, bidis) will continue to be subject to existing high GST rates and compensation cess. This treatment, classifying them as "sin goods" with a 40% de-merit rate (though current rates persist for cess obligations), signifies a long-term policy of disincentivizing consumption. This sustained high tax burden will likely continue to pressure demand and profitability within the tobacco sector.

demand_drivers.description: Double-digit growth in tobacco exports in FY25, driven by strategic policies, increased competitiveness, and wider market access, indicates strong international demand for Indian tobacco products.

new_opportunities.description: The robust double-digit growth in tobacco exports suggests significant opportunities for Indian tobacco manufacturers to expand their global footprint, capitalize on existing market access, and contribute to the national goal of USD 2 trillion in merchandise and service exports by 2030.

market_sizing.methodology: The report highlights that tobacco exports contributed to double-digit growth in India's merchandise exports in FY25, indicating strong performance within the broader export market, without providing a specific market size for tobacco itself.
